page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It features a massive 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 512 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 3,780 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local temporary storage and support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance does not include a GPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 33,062.35 and an overall PassMark CPU score of 89,771.17, placing it within the top 10% of evaluated systems. Multi-core performance is further validated by a stress-ng multi-core result of 73,052.88 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 418.9 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong cached bandwidth of 5,421.5 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 332.26 GB/sec. Static web throughput reaches 110.35 GB/sec, while in-memory operations deliver 117.01 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the inclusion of 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage combined with high RAM density reduces the need for expensive external caching arrays. CPU-bound matrix extensions enable notable CPU-based LLM prompt processing without requiring specialized GPU accelerators. The primary performance tradeoff is seen in single-core compute, where the stress-ng single-core score registers in the middle tier.

The Azure E64ds_v7 is tailored for enterprise memory-intensive workloads, including large relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, distributed data analytics, ETL processing pipelines, and CPU-driven inference architectures requiring substantial memory allocations.
